sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.8954 of 2024
Order:

This Petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India for following relief:
"...to issue a writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus declaring the Lr.No. 33/RW/ACP/Cir20/SLPZ/GHMC/2023 dated 23/09/2023 issued by the Respondent No.4 with respect to the petitioner land acquired to an extent of 1351 Sq.Yrds out of 9946 Sq.Yrds or Ac.2.02 Gts and 120 Sq.
Yrds out of 3733 Sq. Yrds in land bearing Sy.No.44 Part of Gachibowli Village,
Serlingampally Mandal, Ranga Reddy District for laying the road without following due process of law as per Land Acquisition Act, 2013 are illegal, arbitrary and against the principles of natural justice

which are violating the rights under Article 14 and 21 o f t h e C o n s t i t u t i o n o f I n d i a a n d c o n s e q u e n t l y s u s p e n d t h e Lr.No.33/RW/ACP/Cir-20/SLPZ/GHMC/2023 dated 23/09/2023 issued by the Respondent No.4 with respect to the petitioner land acquired to an extent of 1351 Sq.Yrds out of 9946 Sq.Yrds or Ac.2-02 Gts and 120 Sq.Yrds out of 3733 Sq.Yrds in and bearing Sy.No.44 Part of Gachibowli Village.

Serlingampally ::2::
SK, J Mandal, Ranga Reddy District as the said proceedings are illegal, arbitrary and against the principles of natural justice and direct the respondents No.1 to 4 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner as per the New Land Acquisition Act,
2013 with respect to the land acquired to an extent of 1351 Sq.Yrds out of 9946 Sq.Yrds or Ac.2-02 Gts and 120 Sq.Yrds out of 3733 Sq.Yrds to the petitioner for his land situated at Sy.No.44 Part situated at Gachibowli Village, Serlingampally Mandal,
Ranga Reddy District for laying the road in the land of the petitioner without any land acquisition proceedings..."
2.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri M.A.K.Mukheed, learned standing counsel appearing for the respondents and perused the material on record.
With the consent of the both sides, the Writ Petition is disposed of at the stage of admission itself.

3. Having regard to the submissions made by the both sides and perusing the entire material on record, this Court is of the considered view that earlier this Court passed orders in W.P.No.17364 of 2023 dated 06.07.2023 and directing the respondents to consider ::3::
SK, J the representation dated 07.12.2022 filed by the petitioner, in accordance with law.

Now, the respondents passed impugned orders by mentioning the order passed by this Court dated 06.07.2023 and stated that the petitioner has not filed any registered documents along with linked documents.

But, the respondent No.4 has Mohd. Osman Qureshi vs State Of Telangana on 8 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156273787/
1 failed to give finding on each document submitted by the petitioner in the impugned orders.

sentences.text: In view of the same, the impugned order dated 23.09.2023 passed by the respondents is liable to be set aside.

4. Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of by setting aside the impugned order Lr.No.33/RW/ ACP/Cir20/SLPZ/GHMC/2023 dated 23.09.2023 and directing the respondent authorities to consider each and every documents submitted by the petitioner i.e., the documents enclosed along with application from Serial No.1 to 37 by giving opportunity to the petitioner before passing any order within three (03)
months from ::4::
SK, J the date of receipt of copy of this order.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
5. Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall also stand closed.
